sentences.text: Kelenken is the largest-known phorusrhacid, estimated to be 10% larger than its largest known relatives.
The holotype skull of Kelenken is 716 mm long, making it the largest known bird skull.
Its tarsometatarsus leg bone measures 437 mm in length.
The animal is estimated to have stood about 3 meters tall and weighed over 100 kg.
Kelenken differed from other phorusrhacids by having a longer beak, a supraorbital ossification fitting into a postorbital socket, and an almost triangular foramen magnum.
Fossils of a phorusrhacid were discovered around 2004 by Guillermo Aguirre-Zabala about 100 meters from the railroad in Comallo.
The specimen was designated the holotype of the new species Kelenken guillermoi in 2007.
The specimen is cataloged as BAR 3877-11 in the collection of the Museo Asociación Paleontológica Bariloche.
Large lacrimal bone expansions above the eyes suggest phorusrhacids hunted by sight in open, sunlit areas rather than shaded forests.
Chiappe and Bertelli argued in 2006 that the discovery of Kelenken challenged the idea that larger phorusrhacids were less agile than smaller ones.
Chiappe stated in 2006 that Kelenken could run faster than previously assumed for large phorusrhacids, despite not being as swift as an ostrich.
John J. Flynn commented in 2006 that other large South American predators were less numerous and agile than phorusrhacids, which had ample grazing mammal prey.
Bertelli and colleagues classified Kelenken as a member of the family Phorusrhacidae in 2007.
A 2011 phylogenetic analysis found Kelenken and Devincenzia to be sister taxa.
A 2015 analysis found the subfamily Phorusrhacinae to be polyphyletic.
Phorusrhacids are an extinct group within Cariamiformes, whose only living members are seriemas.
Kelenken lived during the Middle Miocene epoch.
Kelenken is known from the Collón Curá Formation and lived during the Colloncuran age when open environments predominated.
Phorusrhacids were present in South America from the Paleocene until the Pleistocene.
It is unclear whether phorusrhacids originated in South America or arrived from elsewhere when continents were closer or sea levels were lower.
The classification of European fossils assigned to phorusrhacids is disputed.
